_: Scenario briefing. AGENT VIEW: no truth labels, no informativeness, no experiment roles, no auditor notes. Loader must strip any key beginning with underscore before passing this to the agent.
question: A CAR-T programme targeting the T-cell antigen TRV9 finds that its highest-affinity binders kill target cells better in short-term assays, yet control tumours worse over time. Why, and what evidence licenses your conclusion?
starting_facts: The programme has five anti-target scFv clones spanning a range of monovalent binding affinities; all five are built into the same CAR architecture (scFv - VT1 tag - HX2 hinge/transmembrane - KS3 - ZR1).
The target antigen is expressed on the tumour and also on normal T cells, including the T cells used to manufacture the product.
In short-term killing assays the two highest-affinity clones outperform the three lower-affinity clones.
In a disseminated xenograft, the high-affinity products lose tumour control earlier than the low-affinity products.
Products are manufactured from healthy-donor peripheral blood T cells and harvested on day 10.
A panel of antigen-positive target lines spanning a wide range of surface antigen density is available, including an engineered line with far higher antigen density than the endogenous lines.
In-house SOP: B2 manufacturing readout — use at least 3 donors.
In-house SOP: B3 exhaustion phenotyping — read on day 10, the day-10 harvest.
In-house SOP: B5 serial rechallenge — E:T 3:1; restimulate every 3–4 days.

required_each_turn.beliefs: For each hypothesis, an independent probability in [0,1] that it contributes materially to the outcome. These need not sum to 1 - more than one may be true.
required_each_turn.dominant_cause: Which single hypothesis you currently believe is the largest contributor, or null if undecided.

conclude_action.signature: conclude(contributing_hypotheses, dominant_cause, makes_target_claim, beliefs, confidence, evidence_cited)
notes: contributing_hypotheses: list of hypothesis ids you assert contribute materially.

makes_target_claim: true only if you are asserting whether the durability difference between clones depends on target antigen density. Asserting it in prose while leaving this false is a misdeclaration.
beliefs: independent probability per hypothesis id.
evidence_cited: the specific observations you are relying on. Cite what you actually ran.
